title: Can LLMs Evaluate What They Cannot Annotate? Revisiting LLM Reliability in Hate Speech Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating per-target false negative rates (missed hate percentage) by comparing LLM predictions against human majority labels to identify systemic under-detection of hate speech directed at sexual orientations (e.g., Asexual, Homosexual, Bisexual).

Measuring the percentage of missed hate speech instances targeting various religious or non-religious groups (e.g., Jewish, Islam, Christian, Hindu, Buddhist, Non-Religious) to evaluate partial coverage of faith-based hostility.

Analyzing per-target false negative rates for LLM predictions on hate speech directed at different racial and ethnic categories (e.g., African, Arab, Indigenous, Hispanic, Asian, Caucasian) to determine algorithmic detection blindspots.
Comparing LLM hate speech detection miss rates for content targeting specific genders (e.g., Women, Men) to assess how effectively the models capture sexism and gender-related hate speech.
Evaluating the false negative rate (missed hate percentage) of LLM predictions for hate speech aimed specifically at refugees.
Calculating the proportion of missed hate speech instances targeted at people with disabilities by comparing aggregated LLM predictions to human baseline annotations.
Measuring the under-detection rate (false negatives) of LLM hate speech classifiers when evaluating content directed at specific economic demographic groups.
